summary.short: Argentine statute approving the protocol amending Council of Europe Convention 108 (ETS 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018. The protocol sets data-protection principles, data-subject rights, transfer limits and supervisory-authority duties for Parties; its entry into force is governed by Art. 37 of the protocol.
summary.long: Law 27699 approves the Protocol amending Convention 108 (ETS 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018 (Art. 1). The amended Convention protects every person, whatever nationality or residence, in processing of personal data under a Party's jurisdiction, excluding purely personal or domestic activities. Processing must be lawful, proportionate and limited by purpose, minimisation, accuracy and storage principles. Sensitive data, including genetic, criminal and uniquely identifying biometric data, may be processed only with appropriate legal safeguards. Controllers must inform data subjects, secure data and notify serious breaches without delay. Data subjects may not be subject to significant decisions based solely on automated processing, may obtain the reasoning behind results, and may object and seek rectification. Controllers must demonstrate compliance, assess probable impact before processing, and minimise risk by design. Transfers to recipients under non-Party jurisdiction require an appropriate level of protection. Parties must establish supervisory authorities with investigation and sanction powers, and a Convention Committee is created. Entry into force follows Art. 37 of the Protocol, which repeals Additional Protocol ETS 181 on entry into force.

notes: Annotates the Spanish translation (CM(2018)2-final, as reproduced by Infoleg) of the Protocol approved by Law 27699; the law itself only approves the Protocol and orders its communication to the Executive. The annexes are published in the BORA web edition and are not in the fetched text; the Appendix on Committee rules is included. No entry-into-force date is stated: Art. 37(1) sets three months after consent of the Convention Parties. Readers should note: Art. 30(3) cites 'Protocolo CETS n° [223]' with brackets, apparently a placeholder; the translation contains OCR artefacts (e.g., 'Proto.ó6íp', 'asegufé^Qt'), and Art. 14(3) refers to 'Artículo 4, párrafo. 3'. Art. 37(2) sets 38 Parties for early entry into force, while the Appendix (para. 2) sets a quorum of 34 Parties in a different context; these are not in direct conflict.

thresholds.note: The protocol sets out data-protection principles, rights, cooperation rules and committee rules for the Convention. It contains no numeric cutoff that changes the legal treatment of persons, firms or public bodies. The numeric conditions it does contain are procedural and are not coded as thresholds: the 38-Party entry-into-force condition in Art. 37(2), the 34-Party quorum in the Appendix, the two-thirds and four-fifths voting majorities, and the time limits in Arts. 30, 31, 33, 34 and 37.
